clue.text: Former Poet Laureate associated with Christmas pudding?

parts.words: Former Poet Laureate associated with Christmas pudding?
parts.note: surface reading: some past laureate with a festive connection
setter's reading: the surname looks like an adjective made from duff, an old word for a boiled pudding, as in plum duff

explanation.walkthrough: Carol Ann Duffy was Poet Laureate from 2009 to 2019; 'duff' is a boiled suet pudding, and adding -y makes a word for 'pudding-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol Ann Duffy held the post of Poet Laureate before Simon Armitage, so she is a past holder of that office.

clue.text: Transplant plants, say, and store

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: to take plants out of their pots
second meaning: a warehouse or storehouse

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a jokey coinage: DE- (remove) plus POT, as a gardener might un-pot a seedling; 'say' admits the word is invented.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a place where goods or vehicles are kept, so it is a storehouse.

clue.text: Stupid couple of articles probing passing fashion

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for a stupid person; the clue gives an adjective

indicators.note: something that probes pushes inside, so these words go into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: the two English articles, the indefinite and the definite

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that a pair of magazine pieces investigating a trend are dim.
explanation.walkthrough: FAD is split after its F to take the two articles: F-ATHE-AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathead is a slow-witted, stupid person, the noun counterpart of the adjective.

clue.text: Raunchy days with girl, embracing grand pathway to heaven or hell?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something within, so the next piece goes inside the words before
raunchy suggests wild, unruly behaviour, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: G is the usual abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A racy weekend with a girlfriend is a road to either paradise or damnation.
explanation.walkthrough: Yggdrasil is the world tree of Norse myth; 'Raunchy' reads as describing the days but signals the shuffle, and 'embracing' adds the grand before it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology the ash tree Yggdrasil links all the worlds, from Asgard of the gods to Hel below, so it connects heaven and hell.

clue.text: Farm attendant fixed soil, removing nitrogen?

indicators.note: removing means taking away, so the chemical symbol named next is dropped from the word for soil

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A farmhand has stabilised the soil, perhaps by stripping out nitrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable lad looks after horses in a stable, a hand who attends to the animals on a farm or yard.

clue.text: Number in G & S, on reflection

indicators.note: in tells us the little word is placed inside the reversed pair
a reflection shows things mirror-wise, so the pair of letters is read the other way round

explanation.surface: A musical item from a Gilbert and Sullivan opera, considered on reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: G & S is Gilbert and Sullivan, whose operettas are full of songs, so the whole clue also points at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a single piece in a musical show, which is a song.

clue.text: Disorder in a handcar — a scorpion?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a scorpion as one example

indicators.note: disorder means things are out of their proper arrangement, so the letters that follow are scrambled

explanation.surface: Chaos on a railway handcar: is a scorpion loose aboard?
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpions belong to the class Arachnida along with spiders, so a scorpion is an example of an arachnidan.

clue.text: Trivial insult son dismissed

indicators.note: something dismissed is sent away, so the letter for the named relative leaves the word

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A minor insult, after which a son is sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: Light reading or a light matter is something trivial and not serious.

clue.text: Most of vulgar physicians beginning to eat variety of fruit

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter is cut from the old word for doctors

parts.note: leech is an old, common word for a doctor, from bloodletting

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

explanation.surface: Coarse doctors almost start to eat a kind of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vulgar' here means vernacular: leech was the everyday old English word for a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: Leechee is a variant spelling of lychee, the Chinese fruit with sweet white flesh.

clue.text: Uncomfortable involving one in effort to confuse

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the word for one sits inside the word for uncomfortable

parts.note: as in by dint of: by the effort or force of

indicators.note: in tells us that combination is placed inside the word for effort

explanation.surface: Feeling awkward, someone joins in an attempt to mislead.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two insertions: one goes into the word for uncomfortable first, and that combination then splits the word for effort, which survives mainly in the phrase 'by dint of'.
explanation.definitionFit: To disorient someone is to make them lose their bearings, so it means to confuse.

clue.text: Again atop rocks in part of South America

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes violently, so the preceding letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Once more, someone stands on top of the rocks in a wild southern landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' looks like a noun in the mountainous scene; it is a verb telling you to shake up the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia is the region at the southern tip of South America, shared by Argentina and Chile.

clue.text: Imagine French are enthralled by Augustus

indicators.note: someone enthralled by another is held captive, so the French word is held inside the name

parts.note: Gus is a short form of Augustus
es is French for are, as in tu es

explanation.surface: Picture the French as captivated by the Roman emperor Augustus.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess is to suppose or suggest without certainty, close to imagining something to be so.

clue.text: Speculation those people kept about soldiers

indicators.note: kept about means held around something, so the people surround the soldiers

parts.note: OR is Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: There is gossip that some group has been holding troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a supposition or hypothesis, an idea put forward on speculation.

clue.text: Former PM in truncated article, leader dropped by Observer

indicators.note: truncated means cut short, so the word for the article loses its end
the leader of a word is its first letter, and dropping it removes that letter

explanation.surface: A cut-down newspaper article about an ex-prime minister, with the Observer's lead missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' looks like the Sunday newspaper, fitting the article; it is just someone who watches.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher was UK Prime Minister from 1979 to 1990.

clue.text: Style of singing that could give you a carol tour

indicators.note: the answer could produce the phrase that follows, so the two hold the same letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A singing style that might win you a carol-singing round of the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloratura is elaborate ornamented vocal music with runs and trills, and the operatic manner of singing it.

clue.text: Fairground attractions free every Saturday at the outset

indicators.note: the outset of a word is where it starts, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: first letters of every and Saturday

explanation.surface: Fairground amusements are free each Saturday, as the season opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground's roller coasters and carousels are known as rides, the main attractions.

clue.text: Musically irregular concoction of harp and disco

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters that follow are blended into new order

explanation.surface: A strange mix of harp and disco music sounds erratic.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is a free-form musical piece of irregular structure, so rhapsodic means musically irregular in that way.

clue.text: Rocks cooling Earth repeatedly from around 30 million years ago

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Rocks cooled on the Earth again and again some thirty million years back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' sits naturally in a geology sentence as a noun; it is a verb signalling a shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oligocene epoch ran from about 34 to 23 million years ago, so the adjective describes that geological age.

clue.text: Left work initially with a Parisienne — very auspicious!

indicators.note: initially says the piece named just before comes first in the line-up

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
port is the left side of a ship
une is the French feminine for a

explanation.surface: A woman from Paris quit her job at the start, and it proved most timely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opportune comes at exactly the right moment, which is very favourable or auspicious.

clue.text: Horse in shock couple of rounds — it's trailing

indicators.note: trailing means following behind, so this piece goes at the end

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A horse in a state of shock after two rounds of a contest, left trailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as in 'she's got it' is sex appeal, SA, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: An Appaloosa is a breed of horse with a spotted coat, developed in the American north-west.

clue.text: Revamped plainer confectionery

indicators.note: something revamped is remade in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sweets that have been relaunched with simpler packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Praline is a sweet made of nuts boiled in sugar, a kind of confectionery.

clue.text: Suggest I should fill job

indicators.note: to fill something is to go inside it, so the letter is placed within the word for job

parts.note: a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: Someone proposes that they ought to take on a vacant role.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward an idea as a basis for argument, meaning to suggest it.

clue.text: Things protecting quiet farming areas — farmer's heading away

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: a word's heading is its first letter, and sending it away removes it

explanation.surface: Hedges guard peaceful farmland while the farmer is away.
explanation.walkthrough: The heading of farmer is F, and that F is the one removed from FIELDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shields are pieces of armour or barriers that protect what lies behind them.

clue.text: Confirm accommodating a boy at a particular time of year

definitions.text: at a particular time of year

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the word for confirm houses the next words

parts.note: to seal a deal is to confirm it

explanation.surface: A booking is confirmed to put up a lad at a certain point in the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonal things happen or are available only during a certain season, a particular time of year.

clue.text: Unusual tense used in this country's English

indicators.note: used in means placed within, so the tense letter goes inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An odd verb tense crops up in British English.
explanation.walkthrough: The tense letter sits inside the possessive for this country, with English tacked on after; the answer is borrowed French and is usually written with an accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, borrowed from French, means unconventional or bizarre, so it is an unusual thing.

clue.text: Performer is associated with time in role (not lead)

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, and not lead means that letter is removed

parts.note: an actor's part is their role
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An actor linked to a period role, though not the lead part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not lead' sounds like a supporting actor; it removes the first letter of PART.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist can be any entertainer or performer, as in a recording artist or variety artist.

clue.text: Spoken sentence provides word for 'herb'

indicators.note: spoken means said out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the term for a sentence

parts.note: time is slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A spoken sentence supplies the word for 'herb'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' looks grammatical but means a jail term, as in doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic culinary plant of the mint family, a common herb.

clue.text: Bit of greenery, perhaps, giving extra heart to another colour

indicators.note: giving something an extra heart means slipping an additional middle letter into it

parts.note: red is a colour other than the green of the definition
the heart of a three-letter word is its middle letter; here it is doubled

explanation.surface: A green sprig gives another colour more heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of RED is E, and an extra copy of it goes into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grassy waterside plant, so one is an example of a piece of greenery.

clue.text: Democrat leading schism in vague movement

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so this abbreviation comes first

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat
a rift is a split or schism

explanation.surface: A US Democrat heads a split inside a loose, ill-defined political movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Drift is aimless, slow motion without clear direction, like a boat drifting with the current.

clue.text: Air not at first gusty, not at first in an unbalanced way

indicators.note: not at first means without its first letter, so the opening letter of the word just before is dropped
repeated, it cuts the opening letter of the second word in the same way

explanation.surface: The air was calm early on, and later the wind blew lopsidedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unequally means not in equal shares, so lopsidedly or in an unbalanced way.

clue.text: Amount of film about flat deserted US city

indicators.note: about means going around, so the film container wraps the next word

parts.note: a can is a round tin of film, as in in the can
D is the abbreviation for deserted, as in cricket and army records

explanation.surface: A reel's worth of footage shot around an empty, flat American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleveland is a large city on Lake Erie in the US state of Ohio.

clue.text: Seeing King flee, make certain to follow

indicators.note: the king runs away, so the letter that stands for him leaves the next word

parts.note: to ensure is to make certain
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: With the monarch gone, someone makes sure of the succession.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result, meaning to follow.
